items.prompt: What are all forms of matter made of?

steps: Atoms are the building blocks of matter.

items.answer: Two or more atoms joined together

items.prompt: In CO2, how many oxygen atoms are there?

steps: The subscript 2 after O means two oxygen atoms.

items.prompt: In H2O, how many atoms are there in total?

items.answer: A substance made of only one kind of atom

steps: Elements contain a single type of atom.

items.answer: A substance made of two or more different kinds of atoms joined together

items.prompt: Is O2 an element or a compound? Explain.
items.answer: An element, because both atoms are the same kind (oxygen)

items.prompt: Is NaCl (table salt) an element or a compound?
items.answer: A compound (sodium and chlorine are different atoms)

steps: Two different atoms joined make a compound.

items.prompt: Why do scientists use models to represent atoms and molecules?
items.answer: Because atoms are too small to see, so models help show their structure

items.prompt: A molecule has the formula CH4. How many atoms of each element does it contain?
items.answer: One carbon atom and four hydrogen atoms

items.prompt: How many atoms are in one molecule of O2?
What is a substance made of only one kind of atom called?

steps: One type of atom is an element.

items.prompt: What is a substance made of two or more different atoms joined called?

steps: Different atoms joined make a compound.

items.prompt: In NaCl, how many kinds of atoms are there?

steps: Na and Cl are two kinds of atoms.

items.prompt: Why do scientists draw models of molecules?
items.answer: Atoms are too small to see, so models show their structure
